clue.text: Young animal's fleshy part

definitions.meaning: the young of a cow, whale or elephant
the muscular back of the lower leg

explanation.surface: A remark about the meatiest portion of a young creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a baby bovine and the muscle at the back of the shin, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Superhuman bishop, a particular sort of Greek

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Ionic Greeks lived in Ionia, one of the main ancient Greek peoples and dialects

explanation.surface: A churchman described as superhuman and of a certain Greek stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Bionic limbs give television heroes powers beyond normal human strength, so the adjective has come to mean superhuman.

clue.text: Opposition about? Subsequently position is held

indicators.note: subsequently means coming afterwards, so the next part follows the first

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for 'concerning, about'

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so one word sits within another

parts.note: a stance is a position or posture

explanation.surface: Someone asks about opposition, then notes a position being held.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistance is the act of opposing something, a straightforward synonym for opposition.

clue.text: They're out to make sure boarders get enough rest

definitions.text: They're out to make sure boarders get enough rest

parts.words: They're out to make sure boarders get enough rest
parts.note: at boarding school the call of a bedtime switch-off sends pupils to sleep; the things switched off are the subject

explanation.surface: A rule at a boarding school to ensure pupils sleep well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lights out' is the bedtime call in a British boarding school; the boarders are pupils living at the school, not lodgers.
explanation.definitionFit: When the lamps are switched off at bedtime the pupils must sleep, so the switched-off lamps are what is 'out'.

clue.text: Namely, something to remove surface marks?

definitions.text: Namely, something to remove surface marks?

parts.note: sc is the abbreviation of Latin scilicet, meaning 'namely'
a rubber is an eraser, which removes pencil marks from paper

explanation.surface: Defining an implement for getting rid of marks on a surface.
explanation.walkthrough: RUBBER is the British word for an eraser; the whole clue also describes a scrubbing brush.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrubbing brush or pad is used to scour marks off floors and other surfaces.

clue.text: Periods in which Tangiers's characters regularly go out

indicators.note: every other letter departs, leaving the alternate ones behind

explanation.surface: Times when the people of a Moroccan city routinely go out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly go out' removes T, N, I, R and S, the odd-placed letters of 'Tangiers', leaving the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages are long periods of time or history, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Speaking at length, making taunt about dead language

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: a dig is a jibe or taunt
Latin is the classic example of a language no longer spoken natively

explanation.surface: A long-winded speaker mocks an ancient tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilate on a subject is to speak or write about it at length, so the participle fits.

clue.text: For instance, someone who brings calm around as a sort of prophet

indicators.note: around means one word is wrapped about the other

parts.note: a soother is one who soothes or calms
say is used to introduce an example, like 'for instance'

explanation.surface: An example of a calming person who is also a kind of seer.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothsayer foretells the future, which is the role of a seer or prophet.

clue.text: A story containing very little that's dynamic

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one word goes within another

parts.note: a lie is a fib or untrue story
v is the abbreviation for very; 'little' signals the short form

explanation.surface: A tale with hardly anything in it that is lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lively and full of energy is a sense of the word, as in 'alive with activity'.

clue.text: Noticing changes, getting round in disguise

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone spots alterations while moving about disguised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is only a link word; 'Noticing changes' reads as a person spotting alterations, but 'changes' is the anagram signal on the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling incognito means concealing one's identity, being in disguise.

clue.text: European bar keeps heavy drinker outside

indicators.note: outside says one word goes around the other

parts.note: someone who 'drinks like a fish' is a heavy drinker
an inn is a pub or bar

explanation.surface: A continental pub refuses to let in a drunkard, leaving him outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Finn is from Finland, a European country, so Finnish describes a European.

clue.text: Arrogant type at university joining society, loose woman

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university, in British usage
tart is a derogatory term for a promiscuous woman

explanation.surface: An arrogant student joins a club and a woman of doubtful morals.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone newly risen who behaves arrogantly, a presumptuous type.

clue.text: Money put into education

indicators.note: the answer is placed within the letters of the following word

explanation.surface: Funding invested in schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: The ducat was a gold or silver coin used across Europe, so an old form of money.

clue.text: Oppressive burden? The old man with little energy inside needs to hang on, we hear

indicators.note: inside means the small piece goes within the other word

parts.note: the old man is slang for one's father, dad
E is the abbreviation for energy

indicators.note: we hear says the next word is chosen for its sound

parts.note: to hang on is to wait

explanation.surface: Father, nearly worn out, must keep going under a heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadweight is a heavy inert load, figuratively an oppressive burden.

clue.text: One coming in settles public grants

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: something that subsides sinks or settles
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A newcomer settles down to receive state funding.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsidies are sums of money granted by the state, public grants.

clue.text: Experiencing big trouble, like Marat finally?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for being in serious difficulty
the French revolutionary Marat was stabbed in his bath, so he ended up literally immersed

explanation.surface: Describing the grim last moments of a French revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean-Paul Marat was murdered while sitting in his bath in 1793.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being in serious trouble, and literally a man in a hot bath.

clue.text: Hot fun, pay having been organised with energy — as a result of this request

definitions.text: Hot fun, pay having been organised with energy — as a result of this request

indicators.note: organised means arranged afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Children's begging brings fiery fun and cash, all energetically arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been organised' rearranges HOTFUNPAYENERGY. Before Bonfire Night (5 November), British children displayed a home-made effigy of Guy Fawkes and asked passers-by for money to buy fireworks.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's plea for coins funded the fireworks, the hot fun of Bonfire Night.

clue.text: English girl joining army, maiden cut out to be a spy

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young unmarried woman

indicators.note: cut out means removed, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as the plain word
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: An English girl enlists but is dropped from the forces to become an agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut out' takes M, the cricket scorebook abbreviation for a maiden over, out of ARMY to leave ARY.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is an agent sent on a mission, sometimes a secret one, so a spy.

clue.text: Like some psychology I read — fun surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that these letters fall into an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Someone reports enjoying reading about psychology.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychoanalysis follows Sigmund Freud's theories, so some psychology is described this way.

clue.text: Great passion shown by Heath? 'Wet', I fancy!

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means imagine, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician called Heath derided as feeble shows burning zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges HEATHWETI. Edward Heath was a British prime minister, and 'wet' was the 1980s term for a moderate Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the most intense heat, used figuratively for extreme passion or fervour.

clue.text: Little bird was first to be given name

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
to have led is to have been in front, first

explanation.surface: A small bird took the lead and was christened.
explanation.definitionFit: A titled person has been given a title such as Lord or Lady, a name of rank.

clue.text: Warrior in army entertained by sailor

indicators.note: entertained by means received within another, so it goes inside

parts.note: tar is a traditional term for a sailor
the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A soldier in the forces is hosted by a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tatars were a Central Asian people famed as fierce horseback fighters.

clue.text: The mourning garb he discarded — rough woollen clothes

indicators.note: discarded means thrown away, so these letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
widow's weeds are the black clothes worn in mourning
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man throws off his mourning dress and puts on rough country wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed is a coarse woollen cloth, and suits made of it are tweeds.

clue.text: In firm, taking a cut as an alternative arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: taking a cut means the word is shortened, losing its final letter

parts.note: steady means firm or stable

explanation.surface: Being in a company and accepting a reduced share as a different deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking a cut' docks the last letter of STEADY to give STEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in place of something else, that is, as an alternative.

clue.text: The Queen in Ireland

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
taken as written

explanation.surface: The monarch visits Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a poetic and traditional name for Ireland.

clue.text: One stealing something from an Assam plantation?

definitions.meaning: Assam in India grows tea, so a leaf picked there

explanation.surface: A thief taking produce from an Indian estate.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang, London's working-class wordplay, the phrase stands for a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang makes it a thief, and literally it is a leaf off a tea bush.

clue.text: Number slightly reduced in citadel

indicators.note: slightly reduced says a small part, the last letter, is lost

parts.note: forty is a number

explanation.surface: A garrison's strength cut back a little.
explanation.definitionFit: A fort is a fortified stronghold, much like a citadel.

clue.text: Rushes endlessly to save vessel in storm

indicators.note: to save means to keep safe inside, so one piece goes within
endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: hurries means rushes
a can is a container or vessel

explanation.surface: Someone races to rescue a boat during a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurricane is a violent tropical storm, a specific kind of storm.

clue.text: Cockney embraced the female office-bearer in church

indicators.note: Cockney speech drops initial H sounds, so both aitches go

parts.note: held means embraced
her refers to a female

explanation.surface: A Londoner hugged a woman who holds a church post.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, famously drop their aitches, turning HELD HER into ELD ER.
explanation.definitionFit: In Presbyterian churches an elder is a lay officer who helps govern the congregation.
